name: WebSocket / Real-Time Event Stream Verification
description: The server's behavior is classified into one of a small set of canonical archetypes (broadcast, private routing, room isolation, idempotent dedup, seq-id replay, capacity limit, connection-count query) and faithfully reimplemented as a real asyncio `websockets` server; the scripted client scenario is driven against it for real, and the actually-observed message delivery / connection outcome is compared against the claimed outcome.

fields.label: Server implementation
fields.help: High-level asyncio-flavored pseudocode describing the server's message-handling logic. Not directly executable as written -- classified into a canonical archetype and reimplemented as real code for verification.

fields.label: Client script
fields.help: Plain-English description of what the named clients do (connect / send / disconnect / reconnect / register).

fields.label: Event sequence
fields.help: Executable scenario grammar: use `->`-separated actions with explicit client names. Supported canonical forms include `<clients> connect|register`, `<client> send|publish 'payload'`, `<client> disconnect|leave`, room `<clients> join <room>`, direct `{to:target,text:payload}`, sequence replay `server emits seq A-B total -> client reconnects with last_seen_seq_id=N`, and count `<client> ask|request count`. Keep observations out of the action chain. Legacy prose is best-effort only.

fields.label: Connection scenario
fields.help: Short scenario category tag, e.g. "drop and reconnect mid-stream", "capacity limit exceeded".

fields.label: Expected message order / state
fields.help: Exact claim over the simulated result. Prefer canonical forms such as `Every client receives alpha, then beta in that order.`, `only B receives the message; C receives nothing`, `client A receives only seq 3-5`, `A receives connections=2 then connections=1`, or `applied-values list ends up as [x, y]`. Include every query reply or delivery whose order matters.
